Re-gate after rework1. Independently re-read docs/agents/design/REQ-031.md in full at commit 0e218ce (not CODE-DESIGNER's result.summary in handoffs/WF02-REQ-031/step-01-code-designer-rework1.json), diffed it against the FAILed version (6c127e2) via `git diff 6c127e2 0e218ce -- docs/agents/design/REQ-031.md`, and re-verified docs/agents/design/REQ-031-schema.md is byte-identical to the version this gate already passed (`git diff 6c127e2 0e218ce -- docs/agents/design/REQ-031-schema.md` returns empty). Per this project's efficient-re-gate convention, effort focused on the changed sections (Sec1.2, Sec3.1, Sec6.3, Sec6.4, Sec7, Sec8's AC3 row) plus the new-edge-case sweep the rework instruction called for; Sec0/Sec2/Sec4/Sec5/Sec6.1/Sec6.2/Sec6.5/Sec9/Sec10 were not re-reviewed since the diff shows them byte-unchanged from the already-passed version.

Original failure re-walked against the fix: liked answered -> improve prompt now current (Sec2.2 ordering) -> respondent scrolls back and replies to the OLD, already-answered liked force_reply message instead of the current improve prompt. Trace through the current Sec6.3: step 3 parses the OLD message's own two lines via parseFeedbackReplyContext, yielding parsed.field = 'liked' (the field that specific prompt was actually for, now that Sec3.1's formatFeedbackTextPrompt renders a second 'Feedback field: <field>' line alongside the existing 'Feedback ref: ' line). Step 7 derives step fresh from DB state = { kind: 'feedback-field', field: 'improve' } (liked already resolved, per Sec2.2's table, unchanged). Step 8's gate now has three clauses; the new third clause 'step.field !== parsed.field' evaluates improve !== liked = true -> no-op, return. This is the correct outcome -- the stale reply is silently ignored rather than being written into 'improve'. Step 8's own prose no longer over-claims: it explicitly names this exact scenario as the case the third clause exists to catch, rather than asserting a guarantee it doesn't implement (the defect in the FAILed version).

Signature/type consistency checked directly, not assumed: formatFeedbackTextPrompt's field: FeedbackOptionalField param (Sec3.1) is threaded through Sec6.4 step 3 ('formatFeedbackTextPrompt called with step.field as its own field argument, so the ref line's Feedback field: value always matches the field the prompt currently being sent is actually for') -- so every freshly-sent prompt's own ref line is self-consistent with the field it is actually for, which is the precondition parseFeedbackReplyContext/step 8 depend on. ParseFeedbackReplyResult's ok:true variant now carries field: FeedbackOptionalField (Sec3.1), and parseFeedbackReplyContext's rule requires that value to equal exactly one of the three FeedbackOptionalField literals or return ok:false -- fully specified, no TBD.

New edge cases named in the rework task, each checked against the actual text (not assumed safe):
1. Field-line-text collision with genuine user reply content: parseFeedbackReplyContext operates on ctx.message.reply_to_message.text (Sec6.3 step 2-3) -- the text of the message being REPLIED TO, which by construction (Sec3.1: 'used for the liked/improve/topicVotes prompts only') is always a bot-authored force_reply prompt, never user-supplied text. A respondent's own reply text is never fed into this parser, so a user typing a string that happens to contain 'Feedback field: X' cannot forge or collide with the anchor line -- the parser never looks at what the user wrote, only at what the bot's own prompt said. No gap.
2. Overlapping/ambiguous field-name strings between two optional fields: the three FeedbackOptionalField literals ('liked' | 'improve' | 'topicVotes') are disjoint exact strings; parseFeedbackReplyContext requires an exact-match (trimmed) equality to one of the three literals (Sec3.1's rule, unchanged shape from the rework, now applied to a second line) -- no substring/prefix overlap exists between them (none is a prefix or suffix of another), so no two fields can be confused by this encoding.
3. nps's reply path: nps is answered only via inline keyboard (Sec3.2), never via force_reply/text reply -- Sec3.1 explicitly states the ref/field-line prompts are 'used for the liked/improve/topicVotes prompts only... never for nps.' formatFeedbackTextPrompt's field parameter is typed FeedbackOptionalField, which structurally excludes 'nps' as a possible value, so an nps prompt can never carry a 'Feedback field: nps' line in the first place, and Sec6.3 step 8's unchanged second clause (step.field === 'nps' -> no-op) remains a defensive belt-and-suspenders check on the determineFeedbackFlowStep side, not the only thing preventing nps from reaching this path. Confirmed unaffected by the rework, as claimed.

Re-verified docs/agents/design/REQ-031-schema.md needs no changes as a result of this design-only fix: `git diff` confirms zero lines changed since the version this gate already passed independently; the field name lives only in the force_reply prompt's message text (Sec3.1), never in a stored column -- FeedbackRecord (Sec2.2) and the feedback table (schema Sec1) are both unchanged and still match column-for-column. Consistent with CODE-DESIGNER's own rework1 handoff statement that no schema change was needed, independently confirmed here rather than taken on trust.

All checks from the original Step 1b pass (AC1/AC2/AC4/AC5/AC6/AC7 mapping, S1 consent precedence, REQ-019-vs-REQ-030 precedent departure, DATA-DESIGNER's three non-blocking MINOR open questions, no design-system token references, no implementation code, no TBD language, full prop/type specification) still hold -- none of the untouched sections that carried those properties were modified by this rework, confirmed by the diff being scoped exactly to Sec1.2/Sec3.1/Sec6.3/Sec6.4/Sec7/Sec8's AC3 row.

No new issues found. PASS.
